plan: 2 Chronicles 36:2-4; 2 Kings 23:31-35, 36-37; 2 Chronicles 36:5; Jeremiah 22:1-5, 6-9, 10-12, 13-23; Jeremiah 26:1-24; 2 Kings 24:1-4; Jeremiah 25:1-14

readings.title: Yeho’aḥaz Deposed and the Financial Extraction
readings.subtitle: Mitsrayim imposes a massive levy, installing a puppet regime to strip Yehuḏah of its wealth.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 36:2] Yeho’aḥaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three new moons in Yerushalayim. [3] And the sovereign of Mitsrayim turned him aside in Yerushalayim, and imposed on the land <dn>את</dn> a levy of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold. [4] And the sovereign of Mitsrayim made his brother Elyaqim sovereign over Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, and changed his name to Yehoyaqim. And Neḵo took <dn>את</dn> Yeho’aḥaz his brother and brought him to Mitsrayim.

readings.title: The Three-Moon Reign of Yeho’aḥaz
readings.subtitle: The king does evil and is swiftly neutralized by the Pharaoh, triggering a heavy financial penalty on the land.
readings.text: [2 Kings 23:31] Yeho’aḥaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three new moons in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Ḥamutal the daughter of Yirmeyahu of Liḇnah. [32] And he did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that his fathers did. [33] And Pharaoh Neḵo imprisoned him at Riblah in the land of Ḥamath, to keep him from reigning in Yerushalayim. And he imposed on the land a fine of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

readings.title: Elyaqim Reassigned as a Vassal
readings.subtitle: Renamed Yehoyaqim, the new sovereign functions as an extraction tool, aggressively taxing the people to appease Mitsrayim.
readings.text: [2 Kings 23:34] And Pharaoh Neḵo set up Elyaqim son of Yoshiyahu to reign in place of his father Yoshiyahu, and changed his name to Yehoyaqim. And Pharaoh took <dn>את</dn> Yeho’aḥaz and went to Mitsrayim, and he died there. [35] And Yehoyaqim gave <dn>את</dn> the silver and <dn>את</dn> gold to Pharaoh. Only, he taxed <dn>את</dn> the land to give silver according to the mouth of Pharaoh. He exacted <dn>את</dn> the silver and <dn>את</dn> gold from the people of the land, from every one according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Neḵo.

readings.title: Yehoyaqim's Era of Rebellion
readings.subtitle: Beginning an eleven-year cycle of compounding wickedness and rejection of Torah.
readings.text: [2 Kings 23:36] Yehoyaqim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Zeḇiḏah the daughter of Peḏayah of Rumah. [37] And he did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that his fathers did.

readings.title: The Wickedness of Yehoyaqim
readings.subtitle: He rules with a corrupt spirit, doing evil in the eyes of his Creator.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 36:5] Yehoyaqim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim. And he did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>his</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Mandate for Righteous Governance
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH presents a conditional guarantee: establish justice and protect the vulnerable, or the royal house faces structural ruin.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 22:1] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Go down to the house of the sovereign of Yehuḏah. And there you shall speak </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> this word,</dq> [2] <dq>and shall say, ‘Hear </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the word of </dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn><dq>, O sovereign of Yehuḏah, you who sit on the throne of Daviḏ, you and your servants and your people who enter these gates!</dq> [3] <dq>Thus said </dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn><dq>, “Do </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> right-ruling and </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> righteousness, and deliver him who is robbed out of the hand of the oppressor. Do not maltreat nor do violence to the stranger, the fatherless, or the widow, nor shed innocent blood in this place.</dq> [4] <dq>“For if you certainly do </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> this word, then there shall enter in by the gates of this house sovereigns sitting on the throne of Daviḏ, riding on horses and in chariots, he and his servants and his people.</dq> [5] <dq>“But if you do not obey </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> these words, </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> swear by </dq><dn>Myself</dn><dq>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that this house shall become a ruin.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Deforestation of the Kingdom
readings.subtitle: Because the covenant was forsaken for adversarial systems, the choice leaders will be harvested and burned.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 22:6] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the house of the sovereign of Yehuḏah, <dq>“You are like Gil‛aḏ to </dq><dn>Me</dn><dq>, the head of Leḇanon. But </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> shall make you a wilderness, and cities which are not inhabited.</dq> [7] <dq>“And </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> shall prepare destroyers against you, each with his weapons. And they shall cut down your choice cedars and throw them into the fire.</dq> [8] <dq>“And many nations shall pass by this city, and they shall say to one another, ‘Why has </dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn><dq> done so to this great city?’</dq> [9] <dq>“Then they shall say, ‘Because they have forsaken </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the covenant of </dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn><dq> their </dq><dn>Elohim</dn><dq>, and bowed themselves to other mighty ones and served them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Permanent Exile of Shallum
readings.subtitle: The weeping must shift from the dead to the displaced, for the ousted ruler will never see the land of his birth again.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 22:10] Do not weep for the dead, nor mourn for him. Weep bitterly for him who goes away, for he shall never come back nor see <dn>את</dn> the land of his birth. [11] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning Shallum son of Yoshiyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, who reigned instead of Yoshiyahu his father, who went from this place, <dq>“</dq><dn>He</dn><dq> shall never come back,</dq> [12] <dq>but </dq><dn>he</dn><dq> shall die in the place where they have exiled him, and not see </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> this land again.</dq>

readings.title: The Economics of Extortion
readings.subtitle: Yehoyaqim is indicted for building his empire on wage theft, violent oppression, and a total disregard for the poor.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 22:13] <dq>“Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness and his rooms without right-ruling, who uses his neighbour’s service without wages and does not give him his wages,</dq> [14] <dq>who says, ‘</dq><dn>I</dn><dq> am going to build myself a wide house with spacious rooms, and cut out windows for it, panelling it with cedar and painting it in red.’</dq> [15] <dq>“Do you reign because you enclose yourself in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink, and do </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> right-ruling and </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> righteousness? Then it was well with him.</dq> [16] <dq>“</dq><dn>He</dn><dq> defended the cause of the poor and needy – then it was well. Was this not to know </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> </dq><dn>Me</dn><dq>?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [17] <dq>“But your eyes and your heart are only upon your own greedy gain, and on shedding innocent blood, and on oppression and on doing violence.”</dq>

readings.title: The Decree of the Donkey's Burial
readings.subtitle: Stripped of all honor, the corrupt sovereign is sentenced to an undignified disposal outside the city gates.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 22:18] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning Yehoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah, <dq>“Let them not lament for him: ‘Alas, my brother!’ or ‘Alas, my sister!’ Let them not lament for him: ‘Alas, master!’ or ‘Alas, his excellency!’</dq> [19] <dq>“</dq><dn>He</dn><dq> shall be buried – the burial-place of a donkey – dragged and thrown outside the gates of Yerushalayim.</dq>

readings.title: The Collapse of the Cedars
readings.subtitle: The leadership that nested in luxury and ignored the divine voice will be devoured by the winds of judgment.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 22:20] <dq>“Go up to Leḇanon, and cry out, and lift up </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> your voice in Bashan. And cry from Aḇarim, for all your lovers are destroyed.</dq> [21] <dq>“</dq><dn>I</dn><dq> have spoken to you in your ease, but you said, ‘</dq><dn>I</dn><dq> do not listen.’ This has been your way from your youth, for you did not obey </dq><dn>My</dn><dq> voice.</dq> [22] <dq>“Let all your shepherds be devoured by the wind, and your lovers go into captivity. Then you shall be ashamed and humiliated for all your evil.</dq> [23] <dq>“You who dwell in Leḇanon, being nested in the cedars, how you shall groan when pangs come upon you, like the pains of a woman giving birth!</dq>

readings.title: The Ultimatum in the Courtyard
readings.subtitle: Yirmeyahu delivers a final opportunity for national repentance before the Temple suffers the devastating fate of Shiloh.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 26:1] In the beginning of the reign of Yehoyaqim the son of Yoshiyahu, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, this word came from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [2] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Stand in the courtyard of the House of </dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn><dq>, and speak to all the cities of Yehuḏah, which come to bow themselves in the House of </dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn><dq>, </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> all the words that </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> command you to speak to them. Do not diminish a word.</dq> [3] <dq>If so be that they listen and each turn from his evil way, then </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> shall repent of the evil that </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> plan to do to them, because of the evil of their deeds.’</dq> [4] <dq>“And you shall say to them, ‘Thus said </dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn><dq>, “If you do not listen to </dq><dn>Me</dn><dq>, to walk in </dq><dn>My</dn><dq> Torah which </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> set before you,</dq> [5] <dq>to listen to the words of </dq><dn>My</dn><dq> servants the prophets </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> am sending you, even rising up early and sending them – though you have not listened –</dq> [6] <dq>then </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> shall make </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> this house like Shiloh, and make </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Religious Establishment Revolts
readings.subtitle: The priests and false prophets demand a retributive death sentence against the true messenger of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 26:7] And the priests and the prophets and all the people heard <dn>את</dn> Yirmeyahu speaking these words in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [8] And it came to be, when Yirmeyahu had ended speaking <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded him to speak to all the people, that the priests and the prophets and all the people seized him, saying, “You shall certainly die! [9] “Why have you prophesied in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, ‘This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city be dried up, without an inhabitant’?” And all the people were gathered against Yirmeyahu in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [10] And the heads of Yehuḏah heard <dn>את</dn> this, and they came up from the sovereign’s house to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and sat down in the entrance of the new gate of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [11] And the priests and the prophets spoke to the heads and all the people, saying, “A death sentence for this man! For he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your ears.”

readings.title: Yirmeyahu’s Stand of Trust
readings.subtitle: The prophet places his life entirely in the hands of the people, warning them of the bloodguilt that accompanies executing an innocent.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 26:12] And Yirmeyahu spoke to all the heads and all the people, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city with all the words you heard. [13] “And now, make good <dn>את</dn> your ways and <dn>את</dn> your deeds, and obey <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall relent concerning the evil <dn>He</dn> has pronounced against you. [14] “And <dn>I</dn>, look <dn>I</dn> am in your hand. Do with me as seems good and right to you. [15] “But know for certain that if you put me to death, you are bringing innocent blood on yourselves, and on this city, and on its inhabitants. For truly <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent me to you to speak <dn>את</dn> all these words in your hearing.”

readings.title: The Precedent of Miḵayah
readings.subtitle: The elders recall the historical mercy granted to Ḥizqiyahu, legally sparing Yirmeyahu from execution.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 26:16] Then the heads and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, “No death sentence for this man. For he has spoken to us in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [17] And some of the elders of the land rose up and spoke to all the assembly of the people, saying, [18] “Miḵayah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Ḥizqiyahu the sovereign of Yehuḏah, and he spoke to all the people of Yehuḏah, saying, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Tsiyon shall become a ploughed field, and Yerushalayim be heaps, and the mountain of the House like the bare hills of the forest.” ’</dq> [19] “Did Ḥizqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah and all Yehuḏah indeed put him to death? Did he not fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and seek <dn>את</dn> the favour of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? And the Master relented concerning the evil which <dn>He</dn> had pronounced against them. But we are doing great evil against ourselves.”

readings.title: The Execution of Uriyahu
readings.subtitle: Another prophet is hunted down and murdered by the state, demonstrating the severe danger of speaking truth, though Yirmeyahu is protected.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 26:20] There was however a man who prophesied in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Uriyahu the son of Shemayahu of Qiryath Ye‛arim, who prophesied against this city and against this land according to <dn>את</dn> all the words of Yirmeyahu. [21] And when Yehoyaqim the sovereign, with all his mighty men and all the heads, heard <dn>את</dn> his words, the sovereign sought to put him to death. But Uriyahu heard of it, and was afraid and fled, and went to Mitsrayim. [22] Then Yehoyaqim the sovereign sent men to Mitsrayim: Elnathan the son of Aḵbor, and some men who went with him to Mitsrayim. [23] And they brought <dn>את</dn> Uriyahu from Mitsrayim and brought him to Yehoyaqim the sovereign, who struck him with the sword and threw his dead body into the burial-sites of the common people. [24] However, the hand of Aḥiqam son of Shaphan was with Yirmeyahu, so as not to give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.

readings.title: The Babylonian Shift
readings.subtitle: As power transfers to Baḇel, Yehoyaqim's rebellion triggers waves of raiding bands authorized by YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [2 Kings 24:1] In his days Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel came up, and Yehoyaqim became his servant for three years. And he turned and rebelled against him. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent against him <dn>את</dn> raiding bands of Kasdim, and <dn>את</dn> raiding bands of Aram, and <dn>את</dn> raiding bands of Mo’aḇ, and <dn>את</dn> raiding bands of the children of Ammon. And <dn>He</dn> sent them against Yehuḏah to destroy it, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had spoken by <dn>His</dn> servants the prophets.

readings.title: The Unforgivable Blood
readings.subtitle: The systemic shedding of innocent blood during Menashsheh's reign solidifies the decree of removal from the land.
readings.text: [2 Kings 24:3] Only at the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> this came upon Yehuḏah, to remove them from <dn>His</dn> presence, because of the sins of Menashsheh, according to all that he did, [4] and also because of the innocent blood that he shed. For he filled Yerushalayim with innocent blood, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would not forgive.

readings.title: Twenty-Three Years of Deafness
readings.subtitle: Despite relentless prophetic warnings to abandon adversarial idolatry, the nation obstinately provokes their Creator.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 25:1] The word that came to Yirmeyahu concerning all the people of Yehuḏah, in the fourth year of Yehoyaqim son of Yoshiyahu, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, which was the first year of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel, [2] which Yirmeyahu the prophet spoke to all the people of Yehuḏah and to all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, saying, [3] “From the thirteenth year of Yoshiyahu son of Amon, sovereign of Yehuḏah, even to this day, this is the twenty-third year in which the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has come to me. And <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, but you have not listened. [4] “Moreover, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent to you <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, but you have not listened nor inclined your ear to hear, [5] saying, ‘Turn back now everyone from his evil way and from the evil of your deeds, and dwell on the soil which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given to you and your fathers forever and ever. [6] And do not go after other mighty ones to serve them and to bow down to them. And do not provoke <dn>Me</dn> with the works of your hands, so that <dn>I</dn> do you no evil.’ [7] <dq>“But you did not listen to </dq><dn>Me</dn><dq>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“so as to provoke </dq><dn>Me</dn><dq> with the works of your hands, for your own evil.</dq>

readings.title: The Decree of the Seventy Years
readings.subtitle: Because the words were ignored, Baḇel is authorized as an instrument of judgment to enforce a massive cyclical reset.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 25:8] “Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘Because you did not obey </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> </dq><dn>My</dn><dq> words,</dq> [9] <dq>see, </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> am sending and taking </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> all the tribes of the north,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>’and </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> Neḇuḵaḏretstsar the sovereign of Baḇel, </dq><dn>My</dn><dq> servant, and shall bring them against this land and against its inhabitants, and against these nations all around, and shall put them under the ban, and make them an astonishment, and a hissing, and everlasting ruins.</dq> [10] <dq>And </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> shall banish from them </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the voice of rejoicing and </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the voice of gladness, </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the voice of the bridegroom and </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the voice of the bride, </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the sound of the millstones and </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the light of the lamp.</dq> [11] <dq>And all this land shall be a ruin and a waste, and these nations shall serve </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the sovereign of Baḇel seventy years.</dq>

readings.title: The Subsequent Fall of Baḇel
readings.subtitle: Once the disciplinary cycle concludes, the Babylonian empire itself will face absolute ruin for its own systemic crookedness.
readings.text: [Jeremiah 25:12] <dq>And it shall be, when seventy years are completed, that </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> shall punish </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> the sovereign of Baḇel and </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> that nation, the land of the Kasdim, for their crookedness,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>’and shall make it everlasting ruins.</dq> [13] <dq>And </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> shall bring on that land </dq><dn>את</dn><dq> all </dq><dn>My</dn><dq> words which </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> have pronounced against it, all that is written in this book, which Yirmeyahu has prophesied concerning all the nations.</dq> [14] <dq>For they too shall be enslaved by many nations and great sovereigns. And </dq><dn>I</dn><dq> shall repay them according to their deeds and according to the works of their hands.’ ”</dq>
